newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf sees no 1997 provisions for court cases.
newsitem.headline: Wharf sees no 1997 provisions for court cases.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd said on Saturday it does not expect to make further provisions in 1997 for two court cases which the Hong Kong conglomerate is involved in.
"We don't because we expect to win the appeals," executive director John Hung told Reuters.

Wharf said on Thursday it had restated its 1996 net profit to HK$2.24 billion from the HK$2.74 billion figure announced in March to take into account a general provision of HK$500 million for two court cases which the company plans to appeal.

"The provision that we have made is a very general provision because basically we do not believe that we have to pay out anything at all because of the appellate position of these two cases," said Hung.

In March, Wharf said a Hong Kong court had awarded about HK$225 million against the company in favour of Danish finance institution ADS due to omissions by a former director of Wheelock Marden & Co to supply certain information to ADS.
In another case, the United States District Court for the District of Colorado awarded US$125.5 million against Wharf to United International Holdings Inc.

"In the case of the ADS case, in order for us to get into an appellate position we probably have to pay the award first before we can appeal in which case this provision allows us to do that," said Hung.
"But I certainly do not say that there needs to be further adjustment unless the cases in appeal are lost. We are advised by the lawyers that we have very strong grounds on both cases."
Wharf said it wanted to put the contingencies behind it.
"What we think is correct is to put this damn thing behind us so that we can see growth in the future rather than an uncertainty about various things," Hung said.
"We don't have any sort of threats any longer."
